correctness.rationale: For fixed integer n>=2, M>=n and arbitrary simplex sampling p, a new completion at the shifted M-window occurs iff the M−1 common middle draws omit exactly one type i, contain every other type, the old departing type is not i and the newly arriving type is i. This proves the exact independent middle-block/inclusion-exclusion identity, with factor p_i(1-p_i). Along any M→∞ subsequence, rates Mp_i have extended limits: diverging rates contribute at most Mp_i e^{−Mp_i}→0; finite rates give independent Poisson rare counts, and each diverging rate type is present w.h.p. Thus every rescaled entrance limit is G_k(c)=Σ_i c_i e^(−c_i)∏_{j!=i}(1−e^(−c_j)) for k<=n−1 finite rates. The extension to [0,infty]^k has zero-coordinate value zero and infinity faces G_{k−1}; adjoining one sufficiently large finite coordinate strictly raises G, so the global maximum is interior, strictly increases with k, and its derivatives force all coordinates equal via strict increase of c/(1−e^−c). Unique diagonal critical point c_k solves 1/c−1+(k−1)/(e^c−1)=0, giving the exact constant C_k. Construction and all-subsequence uniqueness imply one common type with probability→1 and every rare type Mp_i→c_{n−1} after relabeling; no finite-M uniqueness is asserted. Independent enumeration of actual (M+1)-draw words matched the inclusion formula for n=2,3 and bounded windows. This bounded test does not prove global asymptotics.

value.rationale: Maximizing stationary arrivals into complete expiring windows, rather than maximizing occupancy or minimizing first collection time, is a natural but distinct stochastic optimization target. The sharp 1/M improvement over uniform exponential decay and rigidity of the one-common/equal-rare optimal sampling profile are nontrivial asymptotic structure; a useful exact fixed-alphabet design law.
